hypothesis: If bats occur on almost every island and remote islands have endemic bats, most oceanic island groups have a native bat and most remote groups have an endemic bat.
pass_criterion: At least 75% of a predefined set of oceanic island groups have at least one native bat species, and at least 50% of the groups more than 1,000 km from a continent have at least one endemic bat species or subspecies.
fail_criterion: Fewer than 50% of oceanic island groups have a native bat, or fewer than 25% of the remote groups have an endemic bat.
interpretation: 'Almost every island' is read as at least 75% of oceanic island groups (for example Hawaii, Azores, Canaries, Galápagos, Mascarenes, Fiji, Samoa, Tristan, St Helena). 'Often endemic' is read as at least half of remote groups. Subspecies endemism is counted since Darwin did not distinguish it.

dataset.name: The IUCN Red List of Threatened Species
dataset.publisher: International Union for Conservation of Nature
dataset.why_it_fits: The Red List has range polygons and country/island distributions for all assessed bat species, with native/introduced codes and endemism information.
